types.name: Fenrir::AssetHandle<Fenrir::Image>
types.doc: Names one asset of kind `T` (`Mesh`, `Image`, `Material`, `Shader` or `Model`) in the asset store: a slot index plus the generation the slot had when the asset was made (ADR-0021). Plain data that keeps nothing alive, so components hold it and C# receives it as a value. Once the asset is freed the slot's generation moves on and the handle is stale: it no longer resolves, and users skip it. A default-made handle is empty and never resolves.

types.name: Fenrir::SamplerFilter
types.doc: How a texture is filtered between its pixels and its mips.

values.name: Nearest
values.doc: The nearest pixel of the nearest mip.

values.name: Bilinear
values.doc: Linear between pixels, from the nearest mip.

values.name: Trilinear
values.doc: Linear between pixels and between mips.

types.name: Fenrir::SamplerWrap
types.doc: What a texture does with coordinates outside [0, 1].

types.name: Fenrir::SamplerDescription
types.doc: How a texture parameter is sampled (ADR-0024): its wrap along each axis, filter and anisotropy. The renderer core shares one sampler between parameters with equal descriptions. Default made, it is the spec's default sampler: repeat, trilinear, anisotropy 8.

fields.name: wrapU
fields.doc: The wrap across the texture's width, the U coordinate (glTF's S).

fields.name: wrapV
fields.doc: The wrap down the texture's height, the V coordinate (glTF's T).

fields.name: anisotropy
fields.doc: The most anisotropic filtering taken, 1 for none. The renderer clamps it to what the device has.

types.name: Fenrir::MaterialTexture
types.doc: A texture parameter's value: an image and the sampler it is read with. An empty image stands for the shader's default texture (`white`, `black` or `normal`, from GetShaderParameters), which the renderer binds.
